index_title: CCO-free positive STRONG pure powers on one original named sort
scope: Private B032: exactly ONE Foundations III result and its TPP equation. Expand actual orbital graph connectivity/parity, FULL original sortwise NR2, a uniform positive long-walk threshold and the SAP conversion to an injective typed positive path fixing BOTH distinct endpoints. Graph/RAW walk existence uses no SAP; pure STRONG output uses SAP but no semantic CCO, primitivity, countability, exactness or distributivity. Equality and length-zero walks are proof tools only, never STRONG menu entries or a zeroth STRONG power. Finite complete means finite named language/palettes, not a finite real carrier.
scope_explanation: statement and proof. Actual full-lattice parity obstruction, finite atom uniformization, distinct endpoint guards and SAP injectivization have separate premises.

assumptions.name: Actual finite-language typed symmetric homogeneous source
assumptions.statement: U is a homogeneous complete BINARY relational source on finitely many inhabited named transitive sorts, with finite actual pair-orbital palettes and correctly typed converses. Same-sort diversity atoms are symmetric and irreflexive. G is FULL Aut of the WHOLE original typed source acting on the fixed sort, not a substituted automorphism group of its reduct. Real carriers need not be finite.

assumptions.name: Optional visible strong amalgamation
assumptions.statement: Only for STRONG profile/injective-path realization, the actual finite induced typed age of U has SAP. The SAP and homogeneity provider derives infinite stabilizer orbits and fixes the designated already-injective endpoint images.

assumptions.name: Full original sortwise no relative index two
assumptions.statement: On the fixed named sort a, the FULL lattice of G-invariant equivalences has no interval R<C with exactly TWO R-classes inside each C-class. Neither restriction to an exact sublattice nor exclusion only of a global two-class quotient is sufficient.

assumptions.name: Actual same-sort diversity atom
assumptions.statement: Fix one original named sort a and an ACTUAL nonempty same-sort diversity atom t on it. Its graph has an edge. The source theorem quantifies over such t; if the same-sort diversity palette is empty the assertion is vacuous.

imports.name: SAP injectivization with fixed distinct roots
imports.statement: Select strong_selectors C04/C05: a finite partial diversity diagram homomorphism becomes injective, preserving an already-injective designated vertex set and avoiding a finite forbidden set outside it. Positive STRONG word profiles equal represented endpoints guarded to DISTINCT real points. Actual ancestors use only the SAP source premise, not its separate CCO/NR2 assumptions.

imports.name: CCO-free orbital parity and uniform RAW walks
imports.statement: Select ONLY real_closure C25/C26: FULL original NR2 excludes bipartite atomic components; one uniform threshold gives all sufficiently long represented walks within connectivity, including optional equal-endpoint walks. Actual ancestors use ambient action, symmetry, NR2 and elementary finite math, with NO SAP, CCO, countability or further imports. C27 all-equivalence presentations and C28 CCO distributivity are NOT imported.

definitions.name: Actual orbital graph and ambient action
definitions.statement: The t-graph has vertex carrier U_a and undirected edges t(x,y). Every g in G preserves edges. Connectedness and parity are defined by FINITE graph walks, not by an assumed completion of arbitrary diagrams.

definitions.name: Connectivity C and even-walk Y
definitions.statement: C(x,y) means some finite t-walk x->y; Y(x,y) means one of EVEN length. Length zero is allowed in these RAW graph equivalences to supply reflexivity. Always Y<=C. Neither is assumed exact.

definitions.name: Original diversity connectivity palette F_t
definitions.statement: F_t consists of the original same-sort DIVERSITY atoms c whose actual pairs are C-related. C is G-invariant, so membership is uniform over each actual pair orbital. Equality is omitted; t belongs to F_t.

definitions.name: Positive STRONG powers only
definitions.statement: P_t(1)={t}; P_t(n+1)=P_t(n)*{t}, with literal legal diversity triangles and every index n>=1. There is NO P_t(0) menu. Under SAP the standard associativity/path semantics matches every positive word bracketing. Without SAP this displayed left-associated recursion still defines the upper-bound branch.

definitions.name: Full relative-index obstruction
definitions.statement: The even-walk Y is an invariant equivalence inside C; if all t-components are bipartite and contain edges then [C:Y]=2 EXACTLY. This is an interval in the FULL original G-invariant lattice even when C is proper and Y is nonexact.

definitions.name: Opposite-parity walk lengths
definitions.statement: For connected distinct x,y choose a walk P of length l>=1 and an odd closed walk at x of length m>=3. P and the closed detour followed by P have lengths l and l+m. Two-edge x-neighbour-x walks prepend increments of two.

definitions.name: One uniform positive threshold
definitions.statement: For one actual representative ordered pair of every c in finite NONEMPTY F_t choose N_c=l_c+m_c. Set N_t=max_c N_c>=1. The choices depend on t/source, not on a later pair or length.

definitions.name: Finite formal positive path with fixed endpoints
definitions.statement: For n>=1 let V=Fin(n+1), all formal vertex sorts a and all successive edge labels literal t. Different occurrences are distinct FORMAL vertices even when a represented walk repeats real points. S={0,n} has distinct formal vertices and distinct real images x!=y.

claims.name: Every vertex has a genuine t-neighbour
claims.statement: Choose one actual t-edge and transport its first point to any x by the ambient named-sort transitivity. Its second point is a t-neighbour different from x. Graph edges are symmetric and no loops occur.

claims.name: Actual invariant connectivity and components
claims.statement: Length-zero walks, reversals and concatenation make C an equivalence, preserved by G. Transitivity transports whole connected components onto one another. Each component contains a t-edge by C01.

claims.name: Even walks give a full original invariant equivalence
claims.statement: The same zero/reverse/concatenate operations for even lengths make Y a G-invariant equivalence below C. Within any connected component there are at most two Y-classes: choose one root; endpoint path parity distinguishes at most two classes, and odd closed walks collapse them.

claims.name: Bipartiteness of one component forces it in all
claims.statement: A G-automorphism carrying a chosen vertex to another carries its whole component and its bipartition along. Thus if any component is bipartite, every component is bipartite.

claims.name: Bipartite components create an EXACT index-two interval
claims.statement: In a connected bipartite component, two points in the same bipartition side have an even connecting walk and points on opposite sides only odd walks. Both sides are nonempty by C01. Thus each C-class has exactly TWO Y-classes. Y<C are actual FULL original invariant equivalences, not necessarily exact.

claims.name: FULL NR2 excludes every bipartite component
claims.statement: C05 contradicts A03. Hence every t-component is connected nonbipartite. This is precisely the selected I02 C25 branch; it uses no SAP or CCO.

claims.name: There is a finite odd closed walk at each chosen root
claims.statement: In a connected component, if no odd closed walk existed at root x, every vertex would have a well-defined parity of a walk from x: two parities would concatenate to an odd closed walk. Adjacent vertices have opposite parity, giving a bipartition contrary to C06. Therefore an odd closed walk at x exists; its length is at least three.

claims.name: A two-step backtrack pads by exactly two
claims.statement: Choose a neighbour v of x using C01. Concatenating x->v->x with any walk starting at x adds two edges without changing either endpoint or any old edge colour. Repetitions are allowed at this represented-walk stage.

claims.name: One connected distinct pair has opposite-parity base walks
claims.statement: For x!=y with C(x,y), choose a positive base walk length l and the odd closed walk at x length m from C07. Prepending that detour gives a second x->y walk of length l+m, of opposite parity. Both use ONLY literal t.

claims.name: Every length above the pair threshold is realized
claims.statement: For n>=l+m choose the l base if n-l is even and the l+m base otherwise. The chosen base length is <=n and differs from n by an even nonnegative number. Prepend that many half-count two-step backtracks from C08. This realizes EXACT length n with the same literal endpoints.

claims.name: The finite connectivity palette has actual distinct representatives
claims.statement: C is a union of actual old pair orbitals. F_t is finite and NONEMPTY because t subset C. For EACH c in F_t choose ONE realized ordered pair x_c!=y_c with old colour c. No quotient colours or equality representatives are included.

claims.name: Finite atom choices give ONE positive threshold for t
claims.statement: Apply C10 to each C11 representative pair; take N_t as in D07. Finiteness/nonemptiness makes the maximum finite and >=1. For every n>=N_t EACH representative c-pair has an exact-length n t-walk. This is also the finite-uniformization part of selected I02 C26, with its diagonal outputs ignored.

claims.name: Ambient pair-orbital transport gives every real c-pair
claims.statement: For any actual x!=y of colour c in F_t, homogeneity of the complete source or its defining pair-orbital action gives g in FULL Aut(U) sending (x_c,y_c) to (x,y). It preserves literal t and sort a, transporting the C12 walk of any n>=N_t. The SAME N_t works for every such pair.

claims.name: A represented walk is a homomorphism on separate occurrences
claims.statement: For n>=N_t>=1 and any C13 walk, use the D08 formal path. Its nth endpoint may have been visited internally by the walk; this is harmless because occurrences are distinct formal vertices and only successive diversity edges are specified.

claims.name: The designated endpoint restriction is injective
claims.statement: The two formal terminals 0 and n differ since n>=1; their actual images x,y differ since c is diversity. Hence the path homomorphism is injective on S={0,n}, including n=1. Choose forbidden set Z empty. No injectivity of any other initial images is required.

claims.name: SAP removes all collisions while fixing BOTH endpoints
claims.statement: Apply I01 to the finite diagram and C15 designated set. Obtain an injective realization on ALL n+1 formal vertices, preserving every literal t edge and leaving the two actual endpoints exactly x,y. Infinite stabilizer orbits are derived by the SAP provider, not a new axiom.

claims.name: Every connected diversity atom lies in the strong pure power
claims.statement: By positive path semantics in I01, C16 shows c in P_t(n) for EVERY c in F_t and EVERY n>=N_t. Only actual distinct endpoints are read out. No closed-walk equality survivor enters the STRONG palette.

claims.name: Every positive strong power stays inside connectivity
claims.statement: Induct on the POSITIVE recursion D04. Base t lies inside C. A legal triangle witnessing c in P_t(n)*{t} has x-z in a connected input atom by induction and z-y a t-edge; transitivity of C gives x C y. Since c is diversity it lies in F_t. Thus P_t(n) subset F_t for ALL n>=1, independent of NR2 and SAP.

claims.name: All sufficiently large positive STRONG powers equal F_t
claims.statement: C17 and C18 yield P_t(n)=F_t for EVERY n>=N_t with the ONE fixed N_t>=1 from C12. Threshold depends on t/source only. SAP ensures the stated word profile is the genuine strong product and any equivalent positive bracketing.

claims.name: Empty palette, true equality and finite-carrier boundaries
claims.statement: If the named sort has no diversity atom, the universal statement over t is vacuous. For an existing t, F_t contains t and N_t>=1. Zero/equal-endpoint walks occur only inside C/Y/parity arguments; there is no zeroth STRONG power and no artificial identity menu. Finite graph diagnostics are not claimed to satisfy nontrivial SAP or model arbitrarily long injective paths.

claims.name: Exact scoped source theorem without CCO
claims.statement: Combine C19/C20 for every actual same-sort diversity t on the fixed original named sort. FULL original NR2 supplies nonbipartiteness; finite old orbitals supply uniformity; actual SAP supplies fixed-root injection. No semantic CCO, countability, primitivity, exactness/distributivity or arbitrary quotient symmetry premise is introduced.

overview_notes: All invariance uses Aut of the WHOLE original typed source on the fixed named sort, not a changed reduct group.
The parity interval lies in the FULL invariant lattice and may lie under proper connectivity; exact-sublattice or merely global two-class exclusions are insufficient.
Odd closed walks and backtracks supply represented path homomorphisms. Only after the endpoint diversity guard is SAP injection applied.
No CCO, countability or distributivity enters either selected provider ancestry. Equality is not a STRONG atom and no zeroth STRONG power is defined.
Finite diagnostic graphs test the represented/parity branch; they do not pretend to satisfy infinite SAP injection for all path lengths.

controls.check: Independent bounded graph/permutation computations of represented exact-length walks, even-walk components, actual relative-index-two obstruction and eventual connectedness; bipartite negative controls.
Positive-length/distinct-terminal guards and finite-size injection distinctions. No finite graph is asserted to provide arbitrarily long injective paths or certify SAP/CCO/NR2 of an infinite source.

article_feedback.finding: The finite atomic threshold must be positive and uniform before varying the actual pair or length. Opposite-parity walks of lengths l and l+m, with m odd, yield N_c=l+m; the finite nonempty F_t gives N_t=max N_c>=1.
